title: United Airlines 615
summary: United Airlines Flight 615, a Douglas DC-6 operating from Boston to Oakland/San Francisco, crashed on approach to Oakland on August 24, 1951. The aircraft was cleared for a straight-in approach but the pilot ignored prescribed instrument landing procedures. Instead, the pilot relied on visual reference using the copilot's automatic direction finder (ADF), which threw the aircraft 3 miles off course and below the prescribed altitude of 3,500 feet. The aircraft struck Tolman Peak approximately 15 miles southeast of Oakland, scattering wreckage down the slope. All 50 aboard were killed.
probable_cause: Pilot deviation from prescribed instrument landing procedures, improper reliance on automatic direction finder for visual reference, descent below minimum safe altitude, and controlled flight into terrain.

factors.evidence: ADF navigation gave incorrect position, 3 miles off course
Aircraft descended below prescribed minimum safe altitude
Possible altimeter reading error contributed to altitude misjudgment
Aircraft struck Tolman Peak in terrain impact

events.text: Aircraft approaching Oakland, cleared for straight-in approach
Last radio transmission, aircraft descended below prescribed altitude using ADF guidance
Aircraft crashed into Tolman Peak 15 miles southeast of Oakland in fiery explosion
